clauses: Set up the duel: cards and health; who places where and order; legal sidekick spaces including multizone hero space; when Alice’s initial size is chosen; first player.
answers.answer: The attached operative setup instructions and fighter reference answer the requested setup clauses.

evidence.text: The move value applies to **each** of that player’s fighters during maneuver. Harpies have no health dials; each has 1 health. Other fighters have individual dials. Health cannot increase above the highest number on that fighter’s dial.
| Hero | Starting health | Attack | Move | Sidekick(s): starting health, attack |
| Alice | 13 | Melee | 2 | Jabberwock: 8, melee |
| King Arthur | 18 | Melee | 2 | Merlin: 7, ranged |
| Medusa | 16 | Ranged | 3 | 3 Harpies: 1 each, melee |
| Sinbad | 15 | Melee | 2 | Porter: 6, melee |
1. Choose a battlefield and place it on the table. Each player chooses a hero and takes that hero’s components.
2. Set the hero’s and sidekick’s dials to the starting health above; undialed sidekicks have 1 health each.
3. Each player shuffles their **30 action cards into one separate face-down deck**, then draws **5 cards**.

4. The **younger player** places their hero on starting space **1**, then their sidekick(s) in **separate spaces sharing a zone with that hero**. If the hero’s space belongs to several zones, use any of those zones. Make beginning-of-game decisions when placing that player’s fighters. **Alice’s controller**, whether younger or older, chooses **BIG or SMALL when placing Alice** and displays her size token.
5. The **older player** places their hero on starting space **2**, then places sidekicks under the same rules.
6. The younger player takes the first turn.

clauses: Actions required on a turn; repeating and skipping; when/how enforce 7-card hand limit after temporarily holding 9.
answers.answer: The attached turn structure, maneuver, and hand limit text answer the clauses, including the case of 9 cards.

evidence.text: At the start of Medusa’s turn, her optional special ability may resolve (see below). Then take **2 actions** from **maneuver, scheme, attack**. You may repeat an action, including maneuver twice; **you cannot skip an action**.
1. **Draw 1 card first, mandatory.**
You may hold more than 7 cards during your turn. **At the end of your turn**, discard excess cards to your own discard pile until you have **7**, then the opponent takes their turn.

clauses: Ordinary maneuver: draw/movement order; which fighters move how far; passing friendly/enemy; ending occupied; interleaving movement.
answers.answer: The attached maneuver rule answers the movement and order clauses.

evidence.text: Ordinary movement enters adjacent spaces along connecting lines. You may pass through your own friendly fighters, but **cannot finish in any occupied space**. You may **not pass through opposing fighters**. An effect that moves opposing fighters follows the same rules **from their owner’s perspective**. Apply these movement restrictions to card movement unless that card states an exception.

clauses: How maneuver BOOST works; discarded card effect; who gets movement allowance; defeated sidekick card eligibility.
answers.answer: The attached BOOST rule answers the clauses.

evidence.text: **BOOST movement:** during a maneuver, discard **1 card from your hand** to add its printed **BOOST value** (the small circled number, not its combat value) to the movement value for this maneuver. Each of your fighters receives that allowance. For **any permitted BOOST**, add the discarded card’s BOOST value and **ignore that card’s effects**, whether the BOOST modifies movement or an attack. A card that cannot be played because its fighter is defeated **can still be discarded to BOOST**. Effects may separately permit boosting attacks; boosting is not otherwise a universal option.

clauses: Given an empty deck and mandatory draw 2 while hero and sidekick survive: reshuffle or decline; damage to each.
answers.answer: For two missing mandatory draws with an empty deck, each surviving fighter takes 2 damage for each missing draw: 2 + 2 = 4 damage each; no reshuffle or declined draw.

evidence.text: - With an empty deck, your fighters are **exhausted**. Each time you must draw a card you cannot draw, **each of your fighters immediately takes 2 damage instead**. Do **not reshuffle** your discard pile. A mandatory draw of 2 with an empty deck therefore causes two separate 2-damage events to every surviving fighter, unless hero defeat has already ended the game. If only one card remains, draw it and take the exhaustion damage for the next missing draw.

clauses: Legal targets for melee/ranged: adjacent across zone boundary; nonadjacent same zone; disconnected part of same colored zone.
answers.answer: The attached battlefield and attack targeting rules answer the target cases: adjacency permits either fighter across a zone boundary; a ranged fighter may also target any shared-zone opponent regardless of distance, including a disconnected part; melee cannot target nonadjacent fighters.

evidence.text: One fighter per circular space. Spaces connected by a line are **adjacent**. A **zone** consists of all spaces with the same colored pattern, even if separated on the board. A space showing several patterns belongs to all those zones. Adjacency and shared zones are different tests.

1. **Declare** your attacking fighter (active fighter) and the opposing fighter targeted. Any fighter may attack an **adjacent** opponent, even across zone boundaries. **Melee** fighters may attack only adjacent opponents. **Ranged** fighters may also attack any opponent sharing a zone, regardless of distance or adjacency, including another separated part of that zone.

clauses: When attack action illegal; attacker designation; legal cards for both; defender may decline; reveal timing; versatile classification for other effects.
answers.answer: The attached attack and card-type rules answer the clauses.

evidence.text: You cannot take an attack action without an attack-capable card in hand or without a valid target for one of your fighters.

Attack-only cards are red, defense-only blue, and **versatile** cards purple. Versatile cards may attack or defend and **count as both attack and defense cards for other effects**. A fighter-specific card cannot be used by a different fighter; **ANY** permits any of your fighters. A pure defense card cannot initiate an attack; a pure attack card cannot defend.

clauses: Full combat resolution order; same-timing priority; effect optionality; other after-combat effects; played-card destinations.
answers.answer: The attached combat timing and priority rules answer the clauses.

evidence.text:
1. Resolve **IMMEDIATELY** card effects.
2. Resolve **DURING COMBAT** card effects.
3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.
4. Resolve **AFTER COMBAT card effects**. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects **unless the game has already ended**.
5. Resolve other after-combat game effects, such as a hero’s special ability.
6. Finally place all played cards in their respective **face-up discard piles**.

**Whenever effects share a timing, the defender’s effect resolves first.** Card effects are **mandatory unless they say otherwise** (for example “may”); this can harm your own fighters. Complete them in the printed order. A card whose effects are canceled keeps its printed combat value; the canceled effects do not resolve.

clauses: Value 4 vs defense 4 then effect damage 2: combat winner and reason; attack 4 with no defense: attack damage.
answers.answer: Attack damage is 4 − 4 = 0, so the defender wins combat; later effect damage does not change the combat winner. With no defense card, the defender takes 4 attack damage.

evidence.text:
1. Resolve **IMMEDIATELY** card effects.
2. Resolve **DURING COMBAT** card effects.
3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.
4. Resolve **AFTER COMBAT card effects**. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects **unless the game has already ended**.
5. Resolve other after-combat game effects, such as a hero’s special ability.
6. Finally place all played cards in their respective **face-up discard piles**.

**Winning combat is not winning the game:** the attacker wins combat only if the **attack itself** deals at least 1 damage. If it deals none, the **defender wins**, including a tie of values or a defense that prevents the attack damage. Damage from effects does **not** change this winner.

clauses: Sidekick reaches zero but hero lives: token and played card after-combat effect; hero reaches zero: outcome even with pending healing.
answers.answer: A defeated sidekick token is immediately removed; its played card’s after-combat effect still resolves if the game continues. A defeated hero immediately loses and ends the game, so later healing does not resolve.

1. Resolve **IMMEDIATELY** card effects.
2. Resolve **DURING COMBAT** card effects.
3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.

5. Resolve other after-combat game effects, such as a hero’s special ability.

**A defeated hero immediately loses the duel, and the game ends at once.** Do not continue pending effects to heal that hero or finish the turn. Defeating a sidekick alone does not win the game.
